caption: Position: level bands sliding down through the cube - straight across every face
why: On a cube, a straight line through the box - a level, a tilted plane, a slab - crosses several faces, and on the unfolded net it comes out broken and bent. Position gives each pixel its real place in the cube's box, x, y and z each -1..1 with z up, so straight things come out straight.

Use it for anything about height or a direction through the box: water filling up, a scan sweeping across, gravity, slabs. Its neighbours: Direction is the angle from the middle (for things that flow round); Cube ring is the lid and walls as a well; Position is straight lines and planes.
steps: Position has no inputs or settings. `x` runs west to east, `y` south to north, `z` bottom to lid; `pos` is all three as one vector, for nodes that take a point.
`z` goes into a **Wave**'s x (2 cycles, triangle), with a clock (**Time** times 0.3) as its phase: level bands of light that slide down through the cube.
`x` is the **Palette**'s index, so the colour changes from west to east; the wave is the brightness.
Watch a band cross from one face to the next: it stays perfectly level all the way round.

try.label: Square bands
try.text: the Wave's shape square: hard-edged slabs - water levels in a tank.

try.label: More bands
try.text: the Wave's cycles at 4: twice as many bands, half as thick.

try.label: Rising
try.text: the clock's Multiply at -0.3: the bands rise through the cube instead of sinking.
